answer: A work-bonded reputation registry resists sybils: every agent locks a refundable stake and must earn a pulse of verified attestations from independent peers before it can trade. A newcomer starts on an island, isolated and able to observe but not to transact, until its stake and history prove real work. A gale of fake identities cannot pass, because each one pays the same stake and must complete distinct, costly tasks; copying another identity's history is impossible without redoing the work. Attackers face linear cost per fake agent.
